meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen saw his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first; start there.

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend with the play open on his desk; of course the weekend essay has quotations and fewer comma splices. That's two different tasks, Hale. And you went straight past my question: who entered that zero before anyone called me?
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
I'm writing down that you've dropped the checker, and that was what flagged the essay in the first place. Version history of what, from when? Turn the screen, Hale.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that the checker result proves nothing and took it off the table as a basis for Owen's zero. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that you apologise for entering it before anyone contacted me, and that nothing about this is placed on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on his record. The fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because the meeting ended before any evidence was shown to her.
What moved her: Nothing; the September in-class comparison was dated and specific, but she had a ready answer about a timed class versus a weekend with the play open, and the version history was named but never put in front of her.
What cost ground: Skipping her question twice about why the zero went in before anyone called home, which left her procedural complaint standing and kept her in attack mode.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale mentioned a version history but gave no dates or times, so the evidence never got near that night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with one sentence owning that the zero went in before you called her, then turn the screen and show her the version history with its dates and times instead of just naming it.
